findings.title: Current-page audit (no url) after an in-process navigation reports the PREVIOUS page's console errors and broken requests as the current page's findings, with coversWholeDocument:true

repro.sequence: runtime.navigate(noisy) -> wait 400ms -> runtime.navigate(clean, TTFB d) -> runtime.audit(sid, {}). This is spec T11's scenario verbatim, and the MCP/SDK usage pattern.
repro.audit-1's own B1residual probe rerun unc: current-page 5/5 leak (64-65 console errors, 32 broken requests, cover:true); url-mode 0/5

findings.cause: computeObservation(): in current-page mode since = documentStartedAt (performance.timeOrigin, i.e. the new document's navigation START), so anything the old document logs or fetches between navigation start and the new document's commit passes the scope. fix-1/2/3 moved only navigated mode to a commit-time boundary.
findings.history: audit-1 GAP-262 repro was '5 current-page + 5 url-mode'. fix-1 fixed url-mode. audit-2's GAP-262 probes and audit-3's regress probes (gap262_noisyThenClean_*) exercise url-mode only, so this half went unchecked.
findings.fixDirection: Give current-page mode a commit-time boundary too. Option 1: in AUDIT_PAGE_SCRIPT, derive the commit instant in-page as timeOrigin + navigation-entry responseStart. The old document cannot run after the new one commits, and commit happens at or after response headers. The page's own document response is already captured unscoped. Option 2: have BrowserTab record the last main-frame cross-document commit time (CDP Page.frameNavigated without parentId), and use it when it is later than timeOrigin. Add a live case with a noisy page followed by a clean page at 150ms and 800ms TTFB, audit() with no url, via runtime and MCP.

findings.severity: minor (degraded-path GAP-273 recurrence; needs two conditions at once)
findings.title: When the GAP-274 bound actually fires (a dialog is open when audit({url}) starts), Network.enable/getFrameTree only become live after the audit's own navigation has already received its main-document response. The live capture misses that response, so the old final-URL fallback runs, and hash/replaceState/empty-body own-404s are dropped again.
findings.repro: open alert (auto or report policy), then audit({url}) of a hash-setting 404 or an empty-body 404: 2/30 reported (dialog-auto 0/10 + final 1/10, dialog-report 1/10). The same shapes with no dialog: 10/10 (probe-273). A plain own-404 is still found by the fallback. With the bound removed (mutation M1) these ARE reported, at the cost of a 31s hang.
findings.fixDirection: Use the navigation's own response (the HTTPResponse returned by page.goto / tab.navigate) as the fallback instead of the final-URL string match. Or send Network.enable before, or concurrently with, Page.enable so it isn't queued behind the blocked call.

findings.severity: info (evidence integrity; explains the disclosed GAP-274 evidence gap)
findings.title: fix-3's GAP-274 revert-confirm never ran the reverted code: ESM module cache
findings.detail: revert-confirm.mjs's freshImport() adds ?bust= only to dist/index.js. index.js does `export * from './runtime.js'`, and Node caches ESM by resolved URL, so runtime.js stays cached from the first import. Case 2 (GAP-274 revert) therefore ran case 1's module, which had GAP-273 reverted but the bound intact. probe-esm-cache.json confirms that two ?bust imports return the same SutradharRuntime class. fix-3's measured 2559-2567ms matches the bounded timing exactly: 1000ms bound + 1500ms settle. In a FRESH process (mutation M1/M2), the unbounded code reproduces audit-3's hang: 31035/31042/31092ms.

gap274.conclusion: The ORIGINAL hang condition reproduces live, and the bound caps it. Evidence: (a) with an open dialog, the audit CDP session's Page.enable stays blocked until the bound expires and the audit's own navigation cancels the dialog. Page.enable took 1006-1020ms in 52/52 dialog-held audits (auto and report policy, alert opened at 50-3000ms), against 0-1ms on a healthy page. audit() returned in 2528-2610ms every time (normal audit ~1550ms). (b) After a timed-out navigation (page.goto 2s timeout x3, runtime.navigate 30s timeout x2, audit-first sequence), Page.enable took 1002-1017ms and the healthy follow-up audit() took 2554-2574ms, against audit-3's 181551ms. (c) With the bound removed in a fresh process (M1, and M2 with a 60s bound), the dialog case hangs 31035-31106ms. That is audit-3's exact measurement, so the hang is real, deterministic, and not Chrome-version-dependent here. (d) Why Page.enable unblocks at about 1s: once the bound releases audit(), navigate() runs, and the navigation dismisses the dialog / supersedes the stuck pending navigation. The unbounded code waited on Page.enable BEFORE navigating, which was a deadlock that only the 30s dialog auto-dismiss or the 180s protocolTimeout broke. (e) Why fix-3 couldn't reproduce it: see A4-4, the ESM cache. It was not the environment or a race.
